svg.title: Normal Assumption vs Fat Tails
svg.desc: Return distributions are more peaked and fatter tailed than the normal, and extreme events occur far more often than the normal assumption implies.
svg.text: Returns are not normal — peaked center, heavy tails, clustered volatility
Keep the assumption only after testing
Often 5-10 or more in daily returns
Decays as a power law, far more slowly
Closer to normal at lower frequency,
Correct with t distributions and EVT
Combine t errors, GARCH and EVT
One bell curve explains it all
Two numbers, mean and variance, and you are done
Peaked in the center, heavy in the tails
Same variance, very different tail probabilities
In practice they happen far more often
The normal assumption fits the center and misses the tails — and risk lives in the tails.
Fat tails come from clustered volatility and heavy-tailed shocks.
For daily equity returns α is typically 3-5 —
Part 1 supplement — with this sheet every unit of the curriculum is covered.
